status: IN PROGRESS — 25/30 closed at time of writing
runShape: Review ran in three batches of five targets after twelve container reprovisions killed three all-or-nothing attempts. Remediation ran in waves of four, then two, for the same reason.
instrumentRulesAdded: A mutation is ONE literal edit. A bundled mutation's red is unattributable — it proves the bundle matters, not any member. sqlite's manifest bundled four edits; isolating the fourth found that line completely ungraded, and chasing it found two more mutually-masking guards and a fifth mutation that had been surviving unnoticed.

A guard that survives its own mutation is unreachable, redundant, deliberate defence-in-depth, or graded some other way — and which one must be stated. telegram supplied the fourth case: its no-progress refusal is reachable and directly asserted, but its only available mutation manifests as a LIVELOCK rather than a failing assertion, so it is graded by a positive assertion and a hang was correctly not counted as a red.

Never use the empty string as a mutation's replacement. The revert then searches for '' , matches once per character, and is refused; a discarded error made three subsequent sqlite measurements run against a still-mutated file and produce a plausible wrong number.
Check WHICH gate you ran. An agent reported 'tsc -b clean' and was right — tsc -b does not cover tsconfig.test.json, and CI runs typecheck:test separately, which the change had broken.

wrongPrescriptions.note: Round 17 produced ten more, none caught by any test suite. The running total across rounds 9-17 is 53.

cases.detail: The agent BUILT the prescribed `type === undefined` MAM guard, mutated it, and watched the mutation survive the whole suite — the downstream resource check already rejected the only reachable input. First wrong prescription in the run caught at implementation time by the fixer's own mutation step rather than by a later reviewer. It was also a portability hazard: a server stamping type='normal' would have silently lost all catch-up.

Deleting the file::memory: term keeps the syntactic classification, so `file:store.db` still leaves 0644 — measured. And `file::memory:?cache=shared` becomes a startup failure, because it forces a genuinely in-memory database onto the on-disk arm.

cases.mode: the finding's own premise is false
cases.detail: It states neither shipped driver enables SQLITE_OPEN_URI. node:sqlite on Node 22.22.2 does, so the same config names a DIFFERENT STORE depending on which driver is installed.
A per-entry allowance cannot exist: 50ms over 128 roster entries is 0.39ms each, while one screened match at the ambiguity cap costs 0.4ms.

cases.mode: the fix REFUSES a legitimate value
cases.detail: Adding 'function' to the type enumeration leaves the probe at hop 0, where Express compiles a hop count to (a,i) => i < val — true for every address. So `trustProxy: (ip,i) => i < 2`, a legal hop count in function form, would have been newly refused at boot.

cases.mode: the stated reason is false on its own terms
cases.detail: 'The seam has no error channel' — sqlite and nats both refuse a non-positive limit, telegram records the adjudication explicitly, and core bounds catchup.limit with int().positive().

cases.mode: the prescribed assertion is false by construction
cases.detail: An extra row asserting the three interruption invariants for a short write that does not error: once the writer loops, the compaction SUCCEEDS, so 'pre-compaction records all readable' is false.
Making the fixture longer than the largest negative magnitude is reinstated by any later row with a bigger magnitude.

cases.mode: the named helper does not exist and is the wrong shape
cases.detail: 'Reuse the withDeadline helper listener.ts already exports' — it does not export it, and it REJECTS, which would turn a give-up into a throw, and it does not touch pendingAborts, leaving the wait unreleasable, which is half the filed defect.

cases.mode: the guard is placed on the wrong knob
cases.detail: Validating opts.deadlineMs up front leaves `now: () => NaN` producing a non-finite budget from a finite deadline, still throwing raw.

mutuallyMaskingGuards.note: The shape a single-edit mutation exists to expose. Neither member reddens alone, so a later editor deletes whichever was load-bearing with the suite green.
found: sqlite: reschedule guard vs the three tick checkpoints (deleted)
sqlite: top-of-tick vs post-loop check (one kept)
sqlite: generation bump in connect() vs disconnect() (one kept)
postgres: the agent DECLINED to add an entry guard preemptively, because it would have made the post-wait guard unmutatable

operatorErrors: Landed a capacity registry using import.meta.glob without running typecheck:test; tsc -b passes and CI's separate typecheck step does not. Found by a cross-package agent with no stake in the file.
A 10-minute limit killed a mutation replay mid-run, leaving the file mutated; restored from the .mutbak snapshot rather than git checkout.
An expectFail fragment I guessed did not match the assertion's real text, so the harness refused to count a genuine red. Isolating the mutation showed it grading correctly.
